subject: Post-call: scaling profile & hardware recommendation for Dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: scaling profile & hardware recommendation for Dedicated capacity

Hi Elaine — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + the concrete next steps we discussed so your team can pick a path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). I summarized the numbers you gave and a couple of follow-up questions below so we can put a sizing recommendation in the worksheet I attached.

Recap of what we heard from FintechCo: 
- Target integration: production risk-scoring and conversational support for agents (not customer-facing latency critical).
- Expected steady-state TPS: 12 requests per second during normal hours; 40 TPS peak during batch runs (end-of-day reconciliation).
- Typical prompt mix: 75% short prompts (~60 tokens output / ~80 tokens input), 25% long prompts (avg 800 tokens input + 500 tokens output) for batch analytics.
- Concurrency need: ~120 concurrent sessions (mostly short requests), with spikes up to ~300 concurrent during reconciliation windows.
- Privacy requirements: PHI in payloads (requires SOC 2 / private network options but dedicated isolated pool is acceptable if we provide VPC peering).

Open questions (please reply inline):
1) Can you confirm the % of requests that need streaming responses vs full-batched responses? (you mentioned streaming for agent assist)
2) For long-batch jobs, is 500–1,000 request tokens per job accurate for sizing?
3) Do you have an existing GPU preference from ops (e.g., we need to avoid H100 right now for procurement reasons)?

Initial sizing guidance (high level):
- GPU candidates: A100 80GB (good balance for mixed short/long), H100 80GB (best throughput at high token lengths but more expensive), L4/L40S (cost-efficient for short-token-heavy workloads if quantized).
- Baseline recommendation: 2 x A100 80GB nodes (multi-GPU pool) with dynamic autoscale to cover 12–40 TPS and cache short-prefixes; add GPU-backed workers for batch windows (or burst capacity).
- If you need hard latency SLOs for agent-facing requests, consider 1x H100 per 100 concurrent long-request sessions.

Next steps we agreed:
- You: confirm streaming fraction and long-job token counts (answers to Q1–Q2).
- Us: update the attached sizing worksheet with two paths (cost-optimized + performance-optimized) and a recommended pilot configuration by EOD Monday.
- Ops/Procurement: if there are constraints on GPU families, loop in ops (cc'd).

I've attached the worksheet (redwood-dedicated-sizing-worksheet.xlsx) with placeholders. If it's helpful we can book a 30-min deep-dive with Marissa (solutions) and Sergio (infra) next week to finalize TPS/concurrency assumptions.

Thanks — Ben

Subject: Re: Post-call: scaling profile & hardware recommendation for Dedicated capacity

Thanks Ben — great summary. Quick answers inline: 
1) Streaming: ~85% of short prompts need streaming (agent assist shows tokens as they generate). Long batch jobs are non-streaming.
2) Long-job size: yes, typically 800–1,200 input tokens and ~400–600 output tokens per job. Average ~1,100 tokens total.
3) GPU preference: procurement has a standing preference for A100 (vendor contracts), H100 okay if you can justify throughput improvements; L4/L40S likely not approved for now.

One more note: for compliance we'll need VPC peering and support for customer-managed KMS. Also, do you offer disk-backed KV cache for long-session state? That would help reduce recomputation on long prompts.

Happy to sync next week — Thurs or Fri mornings PST work for us.

— Elaine

Subject: Re: Post-call: scaling profile & hardware recommendation for Dedicated capacity

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clarifications, super helpful. A few quick technical responses and an updated recommendation based on your constraints (A100 preference + streaming fraction).

Technical notes:
- Streaming: Redwood's streaming path preserves prefix KV cache per session so short prompts that stream will still benefit from KV reuse; that reduces steady-state CPU/GPU work by ~15–25% depending on prompt overlap.
- Disk-backed KV: we support a persistent KV cache tier for Dedicated customers (hot in-memory + cold disk-backed) — good match for long-session state you described. We'll include cache sizing in the worksheet.
- KMS / VPC: we support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering for Dedicated; we'll add the required network checklist for your security team.

Updated recommended pilot (cost vs performance):
1) Performance-first pilot (recommended for thorough validation):
   - 2 x A100 80GB nodes (multi-GPU per node) configured with 12 concurrent workers each for mixed workload.
   - Reserved burst pool of 1–2 extra A100s to cover 40 TPS peaks and reconcile batches.
   - Persistent KV cache (50GB hot, 500GB cold) to reduce token recompute for long jobs.
   - Expect baseline RPS for short streaming path: ~10–15ms per-token latencies (depends on model).
2) Cost-first pilot:
   - 1 x A100 80GB node + scheduled batch workers during reconciliation windows (auto-scale to 2–3 GPUs for EOD jobs).
   - Quantization + cache tuning for short prompts.

Sizing rationale (very high level):
- With 85% streaming and the token mix you gave, the workload is dominated by short-session concurrency; A100s with KV cache and aggressive batching give the best balance.
- If FintechCo later needs higher throughput for long jobs, migrating a portion of batch jobs to H100 burst nodes reduces total runtime and cost for those windows.

Action items:
- Ben: I updated the worksheet (attached). Please review and forward to Elaine & ops.
- Elaine: which day next week for a 30-min pilot planning call? Thurs/Fri AM PST were suggested.
- Ops: if you can provide network CIDR blocks and KMS contact, we'll draft the VPC checklist.

Happy to jump on the call and run through the worksheet cell-by-cell.

Thanks — Marissa
